lines: The app ships no composer/autoload.php, so the server registers its generic loader for lib/ and looks every class up in the file system.

A composer/composer.json with config.vendor-dir ".", config.optimize-autoloader true, a config.autoloader-suffix and autoload.psr-4 {"OCA\\ApproveLinks\\": "../lib/"} makes composer dump-autoload write composer/autoload.php with a class map; the code of the app does not change.

Nothing in the app calls 1 route outside OCS. Looked for: a route name or a path in the PHP source and the templates, in 4 files of the frontend source and in the navigation of info.xml. A route stays behind when the frontend stops calling it. A route that only a client outside the app calls shows here as well, unless its method allows requests from other origins (CORS).

psalm/phar, phpunit/phpunit are in require-dev of composer.json. The manual recommends a vendor-bin/ of bamarni/composer-bin-plugin per tool, so that the dependencies of a tool cannot conflict with those of the app.

places: lib/Controller/ConfigController.php:43 OCP\IConfig::setAppValue(): deprecated since Nextcloud 29; Use IAppConfig directly
lines: 1 use in 1 file of the public API that is deprecated in Nextcloud 30 to 32. The text of the tag names the replacement where it has one.
lib/Controller/ConfigController.php:43 OCP\IConfig::setAppValue(): deprecated since Nextcloud 29; Use IAppConfig directly

The app reads and writes its app config in 1 place and registers no config lexicon, which IRegistrationContext::registerConfigLexicon() takes since Nextcloud 31. A lexicon states the type, the default and the sensitivity of each key in one place.
Nothing in the app calls 1 OCS route. OCS is there for clients outside the app, so this is no defect in itself.
